A 20-year-old man is transported to a rural emergency department after a motor vehicle collision in
which he drove into a tree at approximately 25 miles per hour. Paramedics report that he was awake
but disoriented at the scene. His vital signs include a temperature of 97.9°F (36.6°C), blood pressure of
142/92 mmHg, pulse of 80/min, and respirations of 20/min. The patient is speaking but confused,
responds to voice commands, and follows simple instructions. Physical examination reveals multiple
facial and arm lacerations, the smell of alcohol and marijuana, and bruising over the abdomen without
tenderness, distension, or rigidity. Cardiac and lung exams are unremarkable. What is the most
appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Abdominal and chest CT (B) Repeat
neurological assessment prior to imaging (C) Immediate exploratory laparotomy (D) Focused
abdominal sonography for trauma exam (E) Chest radiograph anterior-posterior and lateral (F)
Diagnostic laparoscopy (G) Intravenous contrast-enhanced abdominal ultrasound (H) Diagnostic
peritoneal lavage (I) Observation with serial abdominal exams (J) MRI of the abdomen and chest
 A. Diagnostic laparoscopy
B. MRI of the abdomen and chest
C. Intravenous contrast-enhanced abdominal ultrasound
D. Abdominal and chest CT
E. Immediate exploratory laparotomy
F. Observation with serial abdominal exams
G. Repeat neurological assessment prior to imaging
H. Focused abdominal sonography for trauma exam
I. Chest radiograph anterior-posterior and lateral
J. Diagnostic peritoneal lavage
